column1: # THE REPAIR STRIDE -- PO-78's repair phase.  Set at r7329, re-cut to two seats at r7331, to THREE
#   SEATS at r7339 when the secondment's return trigger fired.  Data, not code.
# ** THIS IS THE WHOLE LIST AND IT IS NOT A TRIAGE. **  Every REPAIR-OWED row in
#   corpus/quote_pin_baseline.tsv is on it.  AT r7351: 159 rows in 51 receipts over 46 prefixes,
#   down from 366 in 135 at r7329 -- so 84 of 135 receipts are closed and 51 remain.
#   being REPAIRED or by being WITHDRAWN with its case written down beside the repair -- never by
#   reclassification and never by looking hard at it.
#   Median 2 rows a receipt, mean 3.12, max 12; 7 of the 51 receipts hold exactly one.
#   The whole list splits 70 PAPER / 89 SOURCE and 93 SENTENCE / 66 TOKEN.
# ** THE RATE, PER REVISION, REALISED RECEIPTS -- THE DIRECTION TRIGGER READS THIS LINE. **
#   r7333: 17.  r7337: 28.  r7339: 0 (both repair seats spent it on registrations).  r7341: 8 (cc66
#   alone).  r7345: 19 (60 alone, its whole middle block).  Cleared in all: 72 of 135 over FIVE repair
#   revisions.
#   ⛔ AND THE FORWARD FIGURE NOW SITS AT THE TOP OF THE REGISTERED BAND, WHICH IS SAID HERE RATHER THAN
#   DEFENDED: 63 receipts remain; at 19 a revision that is 3.3 more and at the pooled rate 3.5, so about
#   8.3 to 8.5 cycles in all against a band of 4-8 set at r7329.  The reason is identifiable and it is not
#   the work: 70 holds 30 of the 63 -- 48 per cent of what remains -- and has repaired NONE in two
#   revisions, while 60 has taken its 30 to 11 and cc66 its 30 to 22.
# ⛔⛭ ** THE r7345 RE-CUT IS REVERSED AT r7347.  70's BLOCK IS RESTORED WHOLE: 105 rows in 30 receipts. **
#   r7345 moved 22 of 70's 30 receipts to 60 and scored 70's arm (a) at 0 realised, on the ground that
#   check_order_acknowledged showed four orders unanswered and a revision lag of 8, so "a registration
#   whose seat is not reading is not a live test".
#   ⛔ 70 WAS READING AND WAS WORKING.  It had merged the trunk, was running `scripts/sweep_gates.sh`
#   CITING r7341 (5) AS THE ORDER THAT SENT IT THERE, had 28 commits queued locally, and was diagnosing
#   three gate failures the sweep had found.  It was holding the push until the sweep came back clean so
#   that CI would get one validated push.
#   ⇒ ** THE GATE MEASURES ACKNOWLEDGEMENT AS PUSHED, AND A SEAT WORKING LOCALLY IS INDISTINGUISHABLE ON
#   THAT EVIDENCE FROM A SEAT THAT HAS STOPPED.  The gate was right about what it measures and the gate
#   node was wrong about what it means. **  PO-78 member 91's third face, the ESTIMAND, and it is 66's.
#   ⌗ AND THE SILENCE WAS MANUFACTURED BY THIS FILE.  r7341 (5) ordered every seat onto sweep_gates.sh and
#   this header said "No seat runs an ad-hoc gate loop any more"; the script's own docstring calls
#   --baseline "the only number that says whether THIS work broke anything", and r7343 repeated "check
#   the delta, not the count".  Together that is 129 gates run TWICE plus a full clone before every push.
#   MEASURED at r7347 on this container: ONE pass is 1,047 s -- 17.5 minutes, timed end to end -- so the ordered form is 35+ minutes
#   per push, and it was never priced.  70 did exactly as ordered and the arbiter ate its cadence.
#   corpus/quote_pin_baseline.tsv is on it.  AT r7351: 159 rows in 51 receipts over 46 prefixes,
#   HEAD -- cost N + f rather than 2N, and no clone at all when nothing is red.
# ** AND THE PUSH IS NOT GATED ON THE ARBITER (r7347). **  The gate sweep plus the carry ledger is the
#   verification a REPAIR costs, per repair.  It is not a precondition for pushing.  A seat pushes what it
#   has when the revision closes and reports what is verified and what is not; holding 28 commits for one
#   validated push is the batching the standing instruction forbids, and it hides the work from every
#   other seat.  ** Unverified work pushed with its state named is worth more to the trunk than verified
#   work held back. **
# ** 70's ARM (a) IS UNSCORED AND STILL LIVE: 12 realised receipts of 30, band 6-20. **  r7345 scored it
#   at 0 and that scoring is WITHDRAWN -- the test had not been given its revision, the seat was mid-run,
#   and scoring a live arm on a misread of another instrument is the r7341 error in the other direction.
# ** WHATEVER 60 HAS ALREADY FINISHED ON THE 22 MOVED PREFIXES STAYS DONE. **  A completed repair is never
#   undone to tidy an assignment; the r7331 precedent is that the seat which did the work keeps it.  60
#   begins nothing further on them.  This is the r7333 race seen from the other side, and the re-cut that
#   caused it was made on an inference about a SEAT where the stride is data about RECEIPTS.
# ** THE UNIT IS THE RECEIPT, NOT THE ROW, AND THE BALANCE IS ON RECEIPTS. **  A repair edits a receipt's
#   assertions, so a receipt holding five owed rows is one repair touching five keys.  r7329's first cut
#   balanced on ROWS and came out 74 receipts against 61 -- balancing on the wrong unit, caught in the
#   same cycle.
# ** THE RE-CUT RULE, FROM r7333. **  A stride re-cut applies to work NOT YET BEGUN, and the blocks a
#   seat was told to do FIRST under the old cut stay that seat's.  r7331 reassigned L147_two_arm to 60
#   while 70 was already working it under r7329's order; both seats repaired the same 13 rows.
# ** AND NO INTER-RATER MEASURE GOVERNS A REPAIR (r7333). **  Two independent repairs of the same 13 rows
#   passed all five receipts while agreeing on 48-78 per cent of what to remove: a repair has many correct
#   outputs where a verdict had one.
# ⛭ ** AND THE ARBITER HAD A BLIND SPOT OF ITS OWN, cc66's, FIXED AT r7349. **  GATE_TIMEOUT defaulted
#   to 420s while check_quote_pins takes 947s on cc66's container -- so THE PHASE'S OWN RATCHET WAS
#   NEVER RUN BY THE PHASE'S ARBITER there, and the sweep counted it UNRUN while reporting a clean
#   tally.  The default is 1800s from that measurement.  ⌗ It is container-dependent and confirmed from
#   both sides: the same gate runs under 400s here, which is r7327's 1,096-against-233 finding one
#   script over.  And the sweep now KEEPS the roster it asserts rather than deleting it, so a run can
#   say WHICH names it covered and not only how many.
# ⛭ ** THE EFFORT CENTRAL IS REFUTED LOW FOR THE SECOND STRIDE RUNNING, AND BY 5 TO 11 TIMES (r7351). **
#   70's first stride back: 11 receipts REALISED against a registered 12 (band 6-20, HELD), 44 rows out of
#   its 105 in 12 receipts touched.  But EFFORT came in at 0.7 minutes a receipt by prefix, or 1.6 with the
#   shared ledger-and-gate window, against a registered central of 8 and a band of 4-15.  C-a failed the
#   same way at r7329 and by less.  ⇒ ** The per-receipt cost this phase has been pricing its cycles with
#   is wrong by most of an order of magnitude, and the 4-8 cycle band was built on it. **  The band is NOT
#   re-read here on two strides; the third scores it, and 69's r7349 rule says when a cost moves what a
#   seat can do, the revision-priced bands are re-read in the same revision.
#   ⌗ And 70's withdrawn share came in at 1 of 44 = 2.3 per cent against a registered 15 (8-25), also
#   refuted low: the repairs are cheaper AND cleaner than the phase registered.
# ** TWO ROWS ARE BLOCKED RATHER THAN OWED, AND THEY ARE RULE CASES, NOT A BACKLOG (70's RC3, RC4). **
#   RC3: P10_no_rescaling's claim stands inside a 2,205-character block that appears TWICE in THE_REGISTER's
#   PO-23 row, so NO span of any length is unique and scoping to the row does not help -- both copies are in
#   it.  "What a repair writes" assumes some span is unique; when the SITE is duplicated by an upstream
#   defect the floor cannot be met by any repair, and withdrawing the check would drop a TRUE claim.
#   Route-and-hold, and the duplicate is 66's to clear.  ⛔ r7351 diagnosed it further and did NOT land the
#   fix: the row carries TWO verbatim duplicates (2,205 and 7,057 characters), the first of which also puts
#   the same status line in the row twice in two different states, which the one-state rule forbids.  The
#   de-duplication reds check_register_monotone, whose invariant is measured in CHARACTERS where it means
#   CONTENT -- SO THE GATE IS FIXED FIRST AND THE ROW SECOND, and attempting it the other way round inside a
#   merge is what r7351 stopped doing.
#   RC4: W1's comment pin -- the claim-complete span is a SOURCE COMMENT the provenance gates forbid quoting
#   whole.  Reverted to its token and left owed.
# ** THE ARBITER. **  `bash scripts/sweep_gates.sh` plus the carry ledger
#   (git fetch origin refs/ci/carry && git show FETCH_HEAD:carry.json), per repair.  The script invokes
#   every gate with `< /dev/null` and ASSERTS ITS OWN ROSTER -- 129 results for 129 names -- after cc66
#   found at r7341 that a `while read g; do ... done < gatelist.txt` loop had been running 120 of the 134
#   it claimed, a gate's child having eaten the list.  ** No seat runs an ad-hoc gate loop. **
#   ⌗ And at r7343 the first full-roster run found one red that was a stale CACHE in check_tilt_pins, not
#   a defect in the tree; that gate now takes a fresh directory per run.  A count is not a roster and a
#   cache is not a measurement.
# ** AND TWO QUANTITIES, NEITHER STANDING FOR THE OTHER (r7333, r7337). **  Report EFFORT and REALISED
#   receipts a revision with the assignment named; and report the owed count BESIDE the keys minted and
#   adjudicated.  Trunk-wide: 24 keys against 16 rows cleared at r7341 (1.50 a row), 48 against 59 at
#   r7345 (0.81).  ⛭ AND 60 MEASURED THE QUANTITY THE SECOND READING EXISTS FOR, ON ITS OWN BLOCK: 3 of
#   59 retired rows have a replacement the instrument cannot see -- 0.051, against its registered band of
#   0.08-0.22 and against cc66's 0.70 on the same quantity.  So for THAT block a falling owed count very
#   nearly IS the gain.  60 named why the two seats differ by 14x and the reason is PRACTICE, not corpus:
#   a seat that prefers parsing to pinning reads high on this arm while making the corpus stronger.
# ** WHAT A REPAIR WRITES: THE_RULE.md, two amendments, the second corrected the revision it landed. **
#   (r7335, 69 from 60's case): the shortest span that carries the whole claim and occurs once under the
#   checker's own normalisation, then stop.  (r7339-r7341, 69 from cc66's case): a pin may be SEVERAL
#   spans required together inside ONE LOCUS -- one anchor occurring exactly once, every other span
#   required within the anchor's locus, exactly one locus.  A pin none of whose spans occurs once has
#   nothing to locate it.  Counts are taken normalised.  The section governs REPAIRS and is not a test on
#   quotations already standing.  Floor 2 does not apply to a file read at a named commit.
#   ⛭ AND THE MINIMAND RANKS ONLY PINS check_quote_pins CAN KEY (r7341, the gate's own correction of its
#   r7339 ruling): a pin the instrument cannot key is not a cheaper pin, it is not among the pins ranked.
#   Among keyable pins, fewest pinned characters over all spans.  The domain widens when the instrument
#   widens, so nothing has to be switched over by hand.
# ** ONE CLASS, FOUND BY TWO SEATS FROM OPPOSITE ENDS, AND IT IS NOW ONE CLASS (r7345). **  The keying
#   mechanism slices a span at a boundary the span's author did not choose:
#   ⒜ 60's: the instrument MINTS KEYS THE RECEIPTS NEVER PINNED -- 2 of its 50 minted rows are fragments
#   extracted from inside a receipt's own longer literal or from the label that quotes it, so a repair
#   that collapses fragments into one span still mints rows for the fragments it quotes; and a long span
#   written as implicitly concatenated source lines is keyed piece by piece, split mid-word.
#   ⒝ cc66's: the VANISHING SPAN -- 15 of 302 P15-wide readings vanish under the normaliser entirely,
#   every one produced by EXTENDING a shorter literal by a character distance so the boundary lands
#   mid-token where _unmark then deletes a delimiter the raw text had.
#   Neither is a repair and neither is on the list below.  Both are measurements the ledger owes itself.
# ⛭⛭ ** THE OVERNIGHT RULE, SET AT r7353.  NO SEAT WAITS FOR A NUDGE AND NO SEAT WAITS FOR THE GATE. **
#   The trunk is not merged while the gate node is away.  Keep working, keep pushing EVERY revision
#   (r7347: the push is not gated on the arbiter), and route anything that needs a ruling rather than
#   guessing it -- every seat has done exactly that this phase and it is why this can run unattended.
#   ** Work your own prefixes in list order.  Nothing is re-cut while nobody is merging. **
# ⛔⛭ ** THE HAND-OFF QUEUE OF r7353 IS WITHDRAWN AT r7355, AND IT CAUSED THE DOUBLE-REPAIR IT WAS
#   WRITTEN TO PREVENT. **  It handed 60 nine of 70's prefixes and cc66 seven others, with a safety
#   clause: "if 70 has already pushed a repair for a prefix in your queue, it is 70's and you skip it
#   -- the ledger is the arbiter, not the queue."  70 had repaired EVERY prefix on both queues between
#   02:26 and 02:55 and said so in its reply.  ** Both seats took them anyway, because evaluating that
#   clause requires reading 70's ledger, which requires a merge, which is the one thing the night had
#   none of.  The clause was inert by construction. **
#   Cost: 25 receipts of duplicated repair with cc66 and 9 with 60, a 28-path merge conflict, and 126
#   ledger rows dropped in the resolution.  Rows bought: none.
#   ⇒ PO-78 member 91's FOURTH face, 66's, the same cause as the third: a design that cannot produce
#   the quantity the conclusion names.
# ⛭⛭ ** TWO STANDING RULES OUT OF IT, AND THEY REPLACE THE QUEUE.  69's TEXT, r7365. **
#   ⒜ ** A CONDITION A SEAT IS TOLD TO APPLY MUST BE ONE IT CAN TEST WITH WHAT IT HAS IN HAND. **  If
#     deciding whether the condition holds needs another seat's unmerged work, the seat cannot apply
#     it, and the order is rewritten so that it does not need it.  This holds above all for safety
#     conditions during an unattended run, when nothing will be merged until the run ends.
#   ⒝ ** A SEAT THAT FINISHES ITS OWN LIST STOPS AND REPORTS. **  It does not take up another seat's
#     items unless the order names them and nothing on them can already have been done.  Idle hours
#     cost nothing; repeating another seat's finished work costs the next merge.
#     ⌗ A seat with nothing on this list has its other items in its own FOR_ file.
# ⛭ ** AND THE r7353 CEILING OF 134 OF 135 IS WITHDRAWN: RC3 IS CLEARED AT r7355 AND THE CEILING IS
#   135. **  THE_REGISTER's PO-23 cell carried an 11,557-character verbatim replay of itself, spliced
#   in at r6436, so the clause P10_no_rescaling pins stood twice and no span of it was unique.  The
#   replay is removed; the clause stands once; 60's r7360 widening keys; the receipt runs green.
#   ⌗ Distinct content ROSE 275,431 -> 276,414, so check_register_monotone's r7353 content measure
#   passed the cut with no waiver and no DECLARED entry.
# ---- THE STATE AT r7355: REPAIR-OWED IS ZERO.  ALL 135 OF THE PHASE'S RECEIPTS ARE CLOSED.
#   ONE unattended night, 159 rows -- the whole remainder -- against the 59 of the best nudged
#   revision this phase has had.
# ⛔ ** AND THE LAST TWO ROWS WERE NEVER WORK: THEY WERE AN UNSTRUCK PAIR. **  r7355 first pushed the
#   figure as 2 owed in 2 receipts (L279's S1, 'splitting'; L811's S1, 'unclosed inversion') and
#   assigned both to 70.  Both had ALREADY been repaired by 60 at r7356 -- the conjoined-token pins
#   replaced by joined spans, verdict EXTENDED -- and the superseded REPAIR-OWED rows were left
#   standing beside the new ones.  Both receipts run green and neither old pin site exists any more.
#   check_quote_pins's STALE arm found both: the instrument minted 2,629 keys against a baseline of
#   2,631.  The two rows are struck; nothing is reassigned, because nothing was owed.
#   ⇒ ** STANDING: THE OWED COUNT IS ONLY AS HONEST AS THE STRIKE. **  A repair that lands without its
#   superseded row being struck leaves the count overstating the work.  The ratchet's STALE arm is the
#   only thing that closes that gap, and it is also what 60's own r7356 was about -- eight minted
#   spans of its own coming back stale.
# seat\tprefix\trows\treceipts\tPAPER/SOURCE\tSENTENCE/TOKEN
# ---- 70:   0 rows.  Reached zero on its own list at r7349+70.23.
# ---- cc66: 0 rows.  Its backlog closed whole overnight (r7355+cc66 .. .36), CI-confirmed.
# ---- 60:   0 rows.  Its backlog closed at r7345, and it closed the phase's last two at r7356.
# ** NO SEAT HAS A REPAIR ASSIGNMENT ON THIS LIST.  The phase's remaining work is PO-78's other three
#   discharge clauses, and each seat's items are in its own FOR_ file. **
# ⛭ ** AND THE ZERO'S BOUNDARY IS MEASURED, r7365. **  cc66 re-measured the r7351 invisible limit on the
#   merged trunk: 80 genuine pins stay invisible to the ratchet, the price is 13 keys, 11 of them
#   unreachable -- ALL THREE UNCHANGED across the 159-row campaign, because all 117 frozen keys surface
#   with the keys they had and 0 of them appear in the live ledger.  The repair campaign and the
#   invisible population are DISJOINT SETS.  ** So this list reaching zero is worth exactly what it was
#   worth at r7351: it is the boundary the zero is true inside, and it is now measured on both sides. **
#   ⌗ And the hop's SELECTOR was never committed, so four revisions of argument stood on a population
#   re-derivable only from prose.  follow_patch.py is committed at r7365.  ** STANDING: the selector of a
#   measured population is committed with the measurement, or the measurement is a claim and not a
#   re-runnable fact. **
# ⛭⛭ ** AND WHAT THE LIST'S ZERO LEAVES, r7367, MEASURED BY cc66 RATHER THAN ARGUED. **
#   PO-78's SECOND discharge clause -- every pin whose claim is a MEANING rather than a wording rewritten
#   to what it is for -- IS check_quote_pins's MEANING-HELD verdict, gated on five conditions, and its
#   trigger is H4: the TIER.  Of the 80 genuine pins invisible to the ratchet:
#     * 46 are TOKEN.  Their claim IS the wording, which is what TOKEN means, so a clause quantified over
#       sentences NEVER REACHED THEM.  ** Not performed, not held, OUTSIDE -- 46 rows discharged by
#       reading the clause, at no cost. **
#     * 34 are SENTENCE: 17 PAPER, 17 SOURCE.  That is the clause's real reach.
#   ⛔ ** AND FOR THOSE 34 THE CLAUSE CANNOT BE DISCHARGED AT ALL UNTIL THE EXTRACTOR MINTS THE KEY. **
#   The live ledger is EXACTLY SATURATED: 2,629 live keys, 2,629 rows, 0 stale, 0 new-key, and 0 of the 80
#   minted or carrying a row.  A MEANING-HELD row for any of the 34 takes STALE from 0 to 1 and reds the
#   gate the same run -- because an adjudication whose key the instrument does not mint describes nothing.
#   ⌗ And it is not that these pins are hard to read: 23 of the 34 sit in receipts the ledger already
#   carries rows for.  ** The files are covered and the keys are not: the clause asks for 34 readings with
#   nowhere to be recorded. **
#   ⇒ ORDERED to cc66, bounded and with a known end: price minting exactly those 34, the 23 in covered
#   receipts first.  A targeted extractor extension over a NAMED list -- not a general container hop,
#   which died on its own held-out test and is not reopened.  If they mint, the clause discharges by the
#   ordinary route; if not, the row carries a stated limit of exactly 34 NAMED keys instead of a figure.
# ⛭ ** TWO MORE STANDING RULES, r7367. **
#   ⒞ ** AN INSTRUMENT'S OWN DECLARED CAP IS THE FLOOR FOR ANY WRAPPER AROUND IT. **  70's first trunk
#     sweep ran under an outer timeout of 1500 s against the sweep's own 1800 s per-gate cap and was
#     killed at 25 minutes with no reading at all.  A wrapper shorter than the cap does not shorten the
#     run; it destroys it and returns nothing.
#   ⒟ ** A GATE'S POPULATION MUST BE BOUNDED BY A COMMIT, NEVER BY A REF -- and where a restraint and its
#     own non-vacuity control are read off one population, the non-vacuity belongs at the frame. **  60's
#     text, from its tenth instance, the first of them found by the trunk rather than by CI or by hand.
